analysis: Docs-only PR. Security-relevant change is in docs/developer/build.md (head lines 249-255): release publication now "registers the exact official build" via the scoped POST /v1/releases, with no per-release hardware qualification or manual approval. Release jobs lose environment approvals and assume trusted repository writers. This conflicts with the canonical model (A-017, T-054, TB-011: independent operator approval of the full CodeDirectory, CI keys cannot approve, revocation row lock). It also conflicts with unchanged base text at build.md lines 320-322 (approvals retained) and with verification.md line 13, which still says App Attest depends on durable build qualification. verification.md was only supplied as head text with no diff, so its changed lines were not identified. Its new-looking claims (lines 15-23: CI registers the official build; connection-control reader does not extend deadlines) are consistent with the build.md change. Integration should check the actual coordinator and release code, e.g. whether POST /v1/releases now writes durable qualification rows, whether the revocation tombstone and generation fences still apply, and the workflow files. Those files are not in this batch, so the behavior change is inferred from docs only. The provider connection-control and diagnostics statements in verification.md are descriptive and claim no authorization change.

findings.detail: The build.md change says publication registers the exact official build through the existing scoped POST /v1/releases, and that "No per-release hardware qualification or manual approval is required". The base text instead gated publication on coordinator qualification. The canonical model (A-017, T-054, TB-011) says an independently authenticated operator approves the signed binary and full CodeDirectory, that CI release keys cannot grant approval, and that publication checks the approval under the revocation row lock. If the release key or a compromised release job now makes a build eligible for App Attest serving, a modified or revoked build could gain serving authorization (A-016) with no human gate. verification.md line 13 still asserts durable build qualification, so the docs contradict each other. Fix: keep the independent approval and revocation-lock check and make release registration unable to satisfy it. Otherwise update A-005, A-017 and T-054 to state the weaker trust root, and treat the release key as a qualification root.
findings.title: Release CI can now register builds as App Attest qualified, without independent operator approval

findings.detail: The new paragraph says secret-bearing release jobs accept signed annotated tags in reviewed master ancestry, or trusted master for dev/manual/recovery runs. It says they use repository-scoped secrets "without environment approval attachments" and "assume trusted repository writers". The base text, still unchanged at base line 320-322, says protected signing and publication jobs keep their existing approvals. A writer who can push to master, or trigger a manual or recovery run, can reach the signing and registration secrets without a second reviewer. Combined with the removed manual qualification step, that compromise yields a registered official build and the release API key (A-005), which feeds the release admission path (A-011) and App Attest build trust. The supply chain is out of scope, but the coordinator-side admission it now feeds is in scope. Fix: restore approval-gated environments for signing and registration, or update the threat model assumptions.
findings.title: Secret-bearing release jobs drop environment approvals and rely on trusted repository writers
